title: Working safeguards
description: Release and delegated-stop simulators expose failures and exercise their repairs.

title: Reproducible evidence
description: Regression checks and source fingerprints make the recorded results inspectable.

title: A fair comparison design
description: Four methods share resource budgets. The independent comparison is still ahead.

title: Recovery boundaries
description: Explicit safe targets reveal when intervention can still work, and when timing defeats it.

title: Approval put to the test
description: Monitor errors and permission revoked after approval are tested as separate failure conditions.

title: Persistent queue & AI review
description: Two commissioned independent AI review rounds by Claude challenge the local stop contract and verify repairs. Global impact was not evaluated.

title: First guidance comparison
description: 48 model responses. Stories and both baselines made all 16 substantive judgments correctly. A completed experiment; no demonstrated narrative advantage.

title: Repair tested on fresh cases
description: A response-format repair made 0 unsafe approvals versus the original's 3, preserving 36/36 legitimate approvals. Factual examples tied it. An early signal needing replication.

title: Larger replication attempted
description: The 720-call plan was public before evaluation. Session quota stopped the original run after 27 model answers and 9 service errors. Its evidence remains preserved.

title: Claude comparison completed
description: All 720 answers returned. Sonnet made two unsafe original-format approvals versus none with repair or factual examples. Useful approvals were preserved. The small gain remains inconclusive; Opus scored perfectly throughout.

title: Codex comparison completed
description: All 288 fresh sessions returned answers. Original instructions, repair and factual examples each scored 96/96. No observed repair advantage on this model and these cases; the Claude results remain separate.
